text: So you put out a rain gauge, it just catches rain and directs it into a measuring tube. And the measuring tube is smaller than the opening at the top. So what happens is, it magnifies it. If you get one inch of rain, and if the opening is 10x the area of the inner tube, then you get 10 inches of height in the measuring tube. So this makes it easier to read small amounts of rain. We can get to hundredths of an inch. But there are errors. So if you leave it out, you get evaporation. In a hot or windy day, it evaporates pretty quickly. So you have to get in there and measure it. And then the other error is wind. If you get strong winds, they will actually blow rain over the mouth of the gauge. And then you underestimate the rain. And that's the two big errors.
